samples.summary: Change bundles a large login-hardening epic on top of its stated scope (#661). The branch's own notes admit it: "The branch carries two bodies of work: its stated scope (#661 — the CLI error envelope as one line carrying `command`) and a CLI login-hardening epic layered on top". Beyond #661 the diff also adds `__Host-` prefixing of session/refresh cookies (a forced re-login for every existing production session), a new `cliLoginAvailable()` refusal gate, an HMAC-bound `?confirm=` token, a brand-new `packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts` redaction module, a loopback launch-token indirection plus an on-disk `login-url.txt`, and a frontend login-error rewrite. Mixing security-critical auth/cookie semantics with CLI output formatting in one PR makes each part harder to review and to revert independently.

`COOKIE_SECURE` is introduced by this change as a first-class operator knob — it is read first by `isSecureCookie()`, it is named in the guard's user-facing 400 message and in the new warning, and backend.md prose references it five times — but it has no row in backend.md's Environment Variables table. Operators reading the canonical env contract cannot discover the one variable that now decides cookie `Secure`, `__Host-` naming and whether `wafflebase login` works at all.
samples.evidence: backend.md prose at :155, :163, :172, :445, :486 references COOKIE_SECURE; the env table (rows around :754-:770) lists OAUTH_STATE_SECRET, GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, NODE_ENV, LOG_LEVEL… but no COOKIE_SECURE
searchedFor: read env-table hunk in the diff

samples.summary: The diff adds an env-table row for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` ("HKDF of `JWT_SECRET`", "set it to an independent value…") but no backend code reads that variable — the only other mentions are prose in packages/backend/README.md. The canonical design doc documents a key-rotation knob that does not exist, so an operator who sets it believes they have decoupled the OAuth state key from `JWT_SECRET` when nothing changed.
samples.evidence: grep OAUTH_STATE_SECRET across the repo matches only docs/design/backend.md, packages/backend/README.md and .agent-review artifacts — no .ts file

samples.summary: Contradiction between the documented `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` default and the new `cliLoginAvailable()` gate. The env table still says the variable is optional with default `http://localhost:3000/auth/github/callback` (a loopback URL, which the new gate would allow), but no code supplies that default — `github.strategy.ts:46` passes it through verbatim and `github-auth.guard.ts:39` reads `process.env` directly and treats an unset value as "no evidence the origin is secure", refusing the CLI login with a 400. A developer or self-hoster following the documented default (i.e. not setting the var) now finds `wafflebase login` refused, and the doc row was not updated to say so.

The branch's own notes admit it: "The branch carries two bodies of work: its stated scope (#661 — the CLI error envelope as one line carrying `command`) and a CLI login-hardening epic layered on top". Beyond #661 the diff also adds `__Host-` prefixing of session/refresh cookies (a forced re-login for every existing production session), a new `cliLoginAvailable()` refusal gate, an HMAC-bound `?confirm=` token, a brand-new `packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts` redaction module, a loopback launch-token indirection plus an on-disk `login-url.txt`, and a frontend login-error rewrite. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. The quoted admission is verbatim at docs/tasks/active/20260820-pr786-conflict-resolution-todo.md:8-10. #661's acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:56-63) cover only the single-line envelope, the `command` field, and unchanged code/message. The login-hardening work is a distinct task with its own problem statement, plan, out-of-scope list and acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:1-133,135-163), and it openly states it "rides the #661 branch again (PR #786), not a separate one" (lines 24-30). The specific bundled items all exist: `__Host-` prefixing of session/refresh cookies in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:33,157,343,354,409 (with a comment about cookies written before the change, i.e. the forced re-login); `cliLoginAvailable` in packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts and cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts; the HMAC-bound `wafflebase_cli_confirm`/`?confirm=` token in packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts; the new packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts(+spec); `armLaunch`/`announceLoginUrl`/`login-url.txt` in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts; and packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx for the `?error=login_state` path. The branch's own rationale for co-locating the epics is a design decision the reviewer may contest, not a guard or an absence, so no refutation ground applies. Scope/approach fit is explicitly in the design-fit lane and this is major by kind (work beyond the originating issue's acceptance criteria, mixing auth/cookie semantics with CLI output formatting).

verdict.reason: The literal table gap exists (docs/design/backend.md:751-770 has no COOKIE_SECURE row), but the finding's substantive claim — that operators cannot discover the variable in the canonical env contract — is refuted by concrete counterexamples. packages/backend/README.md:54-70 documents COOKIE_SECURE as a first-class entry in the package's `.env` template, with optionality, default derivation from GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL's scheme, the NODE_ENV=production fallback, when to set it true behind a TLS-terminating edge, and the warning behavior; README.md:117-127 explains its effect on Secure/__Host- naming and the `wafflebase login` 400. packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:135,140 gives the same operator guidance in the self-hosting guide. Under this lens's design-doc-discipline rule, the canonical subsystem doc WAS updated: backend.md carries COOKIE_SECURE semantics in prose at :155, :163, :172, :445, :486 — no missing or parallel doc. Furthermore backend.md's table is non-exhaustive by existing convention: it omits GITHUB_AUTHORIZATION_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN_URL, GITHUB_USER_PROFILE_URL, GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL, FILE_STORAGE_*, IMAGE_STORAGE_*, YORKIE_*, and WAFFLEBASE_KAFKA_*/STARROCKS_DSN, all of which live only in packages/backend/README.md:42-114. So a variable documented in the README template but absent from that design-doc table is the repo's normal state, not a spec/fit violation. Adding the row is a documentation-completeness preference — minor under this rubric, non-blocking.

finding.summary: The diff adds an env-table row for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` ("HKDF of `JWT_SECRET`", "set it to an independent value…") but no backend code reads that variable — the only other mentions are prose in packages/backend/README.md. The canonical design doc documents a key-rotation knob that does not exist, so an operator who sets it believes they have decoupled the OAuth state key from `JWT_SECRET` when nothing changed.
finding.evidence: grep OAUTH_STATE_SECRET across the repo matches only docs/design/backend.md, packages/backend/README.md and .agent-review artifacts — no .ts file

verdict.reason: Verified all three limbs of the finding directly. (1) The env-table row exists verbatim at docs/design/backend.md:757, documenting `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` with default "HKDF of `JWT_SECRET`" and describing it as the key "the OAuth login bindings are signed with", settable to an independent value to decouple `state` from the session key. (2) A repo-wide grep for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` matches ONLY docs/design/backend.md:757, packages/backend/README.md:25, and .agent-review/ artifacts — no .ts file anywhere. Because even a dynamic `process.env[key]` read would require the literal name to appear somewhere, this is conclusive that no backend code consumes the variable. (3) The actual implementation contradicts the doc: packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts implements an unkeyed double-submit cookie scheme — createWebOAuthState() (lines 165-168) uses randomBytes(32) plus hashSecret(), which is a plain createHash('sha256') with no key (lines 266-268); webOAuthStateMatches (lines 177-185) re-hashes the same unkeyed way; the only env reads in the file are COOKIE_SECURE and GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL (lines 229-240). cli-auth.store.ts likewise stores only "SHA-256 of the secret". There is no createHmac, no HKDF, and no key material in the OAuth-state path. So the signing key, the HKDF derivation, and the rotation knob are all fictional; the doc's promised benefit is not just unimplemented but unattainable as framed, and an operator setting the variable gets a silent no-op plus a false sense of key decoupling. This is in-lane under the design-fit rubric's design-doc-discipline bullet: the canonical backend subsystem design doc documents a configuration/architecture surface that does not exist. It is a major-kind fit violation (documented behavior unmet in the canonical doc), not a style or taste preference, and not a line-level logic bug belonging to the correctness lens. No guard, indirect reader, or alternate spelling exists that would render the claim not-present or unreachable.

verdict.reason: The code half of the finding is accurate: github-auth.guard.ts:39 reads process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL directly, cliLoginAvailable() (guard:80-82) refuses when unset, assertCliLoginAvailable() (guard:239-252) throws a 400, github.strategy.ts:46 passes the value verbatim, and app.module.ts:27-29 configures ConfigModule with no defaults/validation schema. docs/design/backend.md:764 does still list a loopback Default. However, the finding's design-fit premise — that the doc "was not updated to say so" — is wrong: the canonical design doc documents this exact behavior at backend.md:148-168, including the no-callback-URL install being refused and the remedies (https GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL or COOKIE_SECURE=true), and line 766 already describes the variable as possibly unset. The self-hoster docs were updated in the same vein (self-hosting.md:132-135; packages/backend/README.md:117-127), and every sample env sets the variable to the loopback URL the gate allows (README.md:126, packages/backend/README.md:41, self-hosting.md:42). What remains is one stale "Default" column cell inside an otherwise-updated canonical design doc — documentation polish, not a failed acceptance criterion, missing/parallel design doc, duplicated module, or Non-Goal breach. Under this lens that is minor, which never blocks.

mergedFrom.summary: Stale comment left behind by the change: `ctx list` still says "The exit code matches `ctx switch`, which still prints prose", but this diff converted `ctx switch` to the JSON envelope. Same staleness pattern the diff fixed in cli.md's Error Matrix parenthetical.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find any counterexample. `ctx list` (ctx.ts:85) and `status` (status.ts:69) both call `outputError(e)` with no second argument, even though their actions are declared `function (this: Command)` so the acting Command is in scope. `outputError` (formatter.ts:158-163) resolves `name = command ? commandPath(command) : ''` and `errorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:129-137) omits the field when it is empty, so these two emit `{"error":{code,message}}` with no `command`. The last-resort attribution in `runCli` (cli.ts:80-99, via the `preAction` hook) cannot help because both actions swallow their throws in a local try/catch — this was the most plausible indirect route and it does not reach them. There is exactly one registration of each command (cli.ts:22-23) and `bin.ts` does no post-processing. Under the design-fit rubric this is a `major` spec-conformance gap: the issue's acceptance criterion "It carries `command` with the dotted command name" (todo lines 59-60) is unmet for these two emitters; docs/design/cli.md:1492-1511 says "one line, attributed" holds for `outputError` commands and names only `login` as an exception; README.md:141-144 states the shape unconditionally; and cli.md:1529 puts `ctx list` and `ctx switch` on the same NOT_LOGGED_IN row while only `ctx switch` (ctx.ts:93,102-106,114) actually attributes. No test guards it (status.test.ts:175-185,230-234 assert only `error.code`).
